title: Calculating a cut capacity
problem: A directed network has source S, sink T, and intermediate vertices A and B: S→A (capacity 8), S→B (capacity 6), A→T (capacity 5), B→T (capacity 7), A→B (capacity 4). Find the capacity of the cut with S-side = {S, A} and T-side = {B, T}.

steps.instruction: State the rule for which edges cross a cut.
steps.working: Identify every edge that crosses from the S-side to the T-side. An edge counts only if it starts on the S-side and ends on the T-side. S-side = {S, A}, T-side = {B, T}.

steps.instruction: Check each edge to see whether it crosses the cut.
steps.working:
S→A: both S-side — does not cross
S→B: S is S-side, B is T-side → crosses (capacity 6)
A→T: A is S-side, T is T-side → crosses (capacity 5)
A→B: A is S-side, B is T-side → crosses (capacity 4)
B→T: both T-side — does not cross

steps.instruction: Add the capacities of the crossing edges.

answer: The capacity of the cut is 15.

title: Finding the maximum flow using the minimum-cut theorem
problem: For the same network (S→A cap 8, S→B cap 6, A→T cap 5, B→T cap 7, A→B cap 4), find the maximum flow from S to T by evaluating all possible cuts.

steps.instruction: List the meaningful cuts (there are 4 non-trivial ways to split {S, A, B, T} into two groups with S and T on opposite sides) and their capacities.
steps.working:
Cut 1: S-side = {S}, T-side = {A, B, T}. Edges crossing: S→A (8) + S→B (6) = 14

Cut 2: S-side = {S, A}, T-side = {B, T}. Edges crossing: S→B (6) + A→T (5) + A→B (4) = 15

Cut 3: S-side = {S, B}, T-side = {A, T}. Edges crossing: S→A (8) + B→T (7) = 15 (A→B goes from T-side to S-side — backward edge, not counted)

Cut 4: S-side = {S, A, B}, T-side = {T}. Edges crossing: A→T (5) + B→T (7) = 12
The cut capacities are: 14, 15, 15, 12. The minimum is 12 (Cut 4).

steps.instruction: Verify that a flow of 12 units is achievable.
steps.working: The only way to get 12 units from S to T is if both A→T (5) and B→T (7) carry their full capacity simultaneously. Working backwards: A→T uses 5 (so A needs 5 incoming); B→T uses 7 (so B needs 7 incoming). Try S→A = 8, S→B = 4, A→B = 3; then B = 4 + 3 = 7 ✓, A→T = 5 ✓. Total outflow = $8 + 4 = 12$ ✓.

answer: The maximum flow from S to T is 12 units.

title: Interpreting the minimum cut in context
problem: A water supply system has source S (reservoir), sink T (town), and two pump stations A and B: S→A (capacity 10), S→B (capacity 7), A→T (capacity 8), B→T (capacity 6), A→B (capacity 3). Find the maximum flow the system can deliver to the town.

steps.working:
{S}: S→A (10) + S→B (7) = 17
{S, A}: S→B (7) + A→T (8) + A→B (3) = 18
{S, B}: S→A (10) + B→T (6) = 16 (A→B is backward here — not counted)
{S, A, B}: A→T (8) + B→T (6) = 14
Minimum cut capacity = 14 (cut through {S, A, B}).

steps.instruction: State the maximum flow and explain the bottleneck.
steps.working: Maximum flow = 14 units per unit time. The bottleneck is the total capacity of the pipes leading into the town — A→T (8) and B→T (6) — regardless of how much the earlier pipes can carry.

answer: The maximum flow the system can deliver to the town is 14 units per unit time.
